A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Robustness of Mixtures of Experts to Feature Noise. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison. Appendix content matches after accounting for table renumbering and citation updates.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic experiments, LLM activation analyses, noisy linear-probing evaluations, T5 robustness experiments, and MiniMind training results, including substantial appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and reports additional cross-block overlap and ImageNet-C experiments in Section 5.

M1.justification: The dense and sparse estimators, expert construction, router training, probing procedure, and MiniMind architecture remain unchanged. Evaluating existing vision architectures and introducing additional perturbation scenarios do not establish a modification to the proposed method.

E1.justification: v2 adds vision classification under ImageNet-C Gaussian corruption, substantially extending the previous synthetic and language coverage. It also adds a controlled synthetic scenario with overlapping feature blocks, testing departures from perfect modularity. Existing datasets and tasks are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 expands the probing comparison from Lasso to Lasso, Ridge, and Elastic Net, adding substantive controls for alternative regularization explanations. The new vision experiment compares sparse V-MoE-B/16 against dense ViT-L/16. The original appendix comparisons against Lasso remain.

E3.justification: New protocols sweep cross-block nuisance magnitude from 0 to 1 before observation noise, using oracle routing, and evaluate ImageNet-C top-1 accuracy at severities 1, 3, and 5. The vision comparison uses 224px ViT-L/16 and 384px V-MoE-B/16 with different augmentation recipes. Existing appendix settings remain unchanged; revised Table 1 values do not establish which probing settings changed.

E4.justification: Table 2 adds sensitivity analysis of the central block-diagonal assumption, testing whether sparse estimation remains advantageous as feature blocks overlap under oracle routing. Table 3 adds corruption-severity robustness analysis in vision. These extend the retained text-perturbation, synthetic-noise, and sample-efficiency analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions retain Figure 9's confidence intervals over 100 seeds, four-run excess-risk fits, and the synthetic tables' seed-specific and plus/minus reporting. The new tables provide point estimates without introducing run counts, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces headline probing values: v1 reports AG News drops of 0.3166 for Lasso and 0.2580–0.2687 for MoE; v2 reports 5.19% and 7.75%, respectively, with all three dense baselines outperforming MoE there. Comparable procedures are not established, and the old values remain in v2 Appendix Table 5. New Tables 2–3 add overlap results and ImageNet-C accuracies, including 59.65% for V-MoE versus 46.57% for ViT at severity 5.

T1.justification: The formal model, assumptions, theorems, derivations, and Appendix A proofs are retained. Theorem 4.3 only changes equivalent transpose notation and equation wrapping. The overlap experiment does not revise the formal block-diagonal assumption or establish a new theorem.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: activation sparsity filters feature noise under equal total parameter counts, improving generalization, robustness, convergence, and sample efficiency. The added experiments support or extend discussion of these retained contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly interprets regularized-baseline comparisons as isolating modular sparsity from regularization, overlap results as robustness to imperfect modularity, and vision results as evidence beyond linear probing. These substantially extend mechanism and applicability interpretations. The vision passage additionally attributes the advantage to routing rather than total capacity, although its reported counts concern active parameters.

D1.justification: v2 documents the new nuisance-injection order and oracle-routing control, vision input resolutions, augmentation recipes, and active parameter counts of 114M versus 307M. Existing appendix implementation details and resource links remain unchanged. It does not supply corresponding Ridge/Elastic Net tuning details or explain how the revised probing table relates to the retained appendix results.

R1.justification: Section 2 replaces detailed Ho/Nguyen estimation-convergence coverage with substantial recent theory on task-dependent scaling, continual learning, optimization, parameterization, expressivity, and mode connectivity. It explicitly positions feature-noise robustness against these directions and adds ImageNet-C and V-MoE references. Publication updates to retained works are bibliographic changes rather than new citations.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in the theoretical related-work paragraph and expanded Section 5 narrative. v2 also adds acknowledgements and updates correspondence and proceedings information. The introduction, methodological exposition, conclusions, section order, and appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Presentation changes are localized: Table 1 replaces four configuration-specific MoE columns with one MoE column and additional baseline columns, using percentage units; two compact tables are added for overlap and vision robustness. Figures 1–9 and existing appendix table layouts remain unchanged apart from numbering and page reflow.

improvement.justification: Additional regularization controls and the overlap sensitivity test address meaningful weaknesses in v1, while ImageNet-C broadens empirical validation. However, revised Table 1 values are unexplained alongside unchanged Appendix Table 5 values, weakening traceability. The vision comparison also differs in resolution and augmentation, and active parameter counts do not establish matched total capacity despite the causal interpretation. These benefits and reporting/inference problems prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
